projects.title: AI Job Scoring Multi-Agent System
projects.overview: The AI Job Scoring Multi-Agent System is an agentic job-matching application designed to evaluate how well a candidate's CV matches a specific job description. The system uses specialized HR and CV agents to structure job requirements, generate evaluation criteria, retrieve relevant evidence from CV documents, and produce evidence-based answers and a final matching score.
projects.problem: Traditional CV screening can be time-consuming and may not consistently evaluate candidates against the specific requirements of a job. In addition, CVs are semi-structured documents, making reliable information retrieval challenging. The system addresses these challenges by combining agentic AI with document retrieval to evaluate candidates according to the requirements defined by the HR agent while grounding answers in the actual CV content.
projects.approach: The system follows a multi-agent architecture in which an HR Agent analyzes the job description and generates structured evaluation questions and criteria, while a CV Agent retrieves relevant evidence from the candidate's CV and evaluates each requirement based strictly on the available document content. For CV document retrieval, three chunking strategies were explored: character-based chunking as a baseline, semantic chunking based on content similarity, and agentic chunking where an LLM helps determine meaningful document boundaries. The resulting chunks are embedded and stored in ChromaDB for retrieval through LangChain. A React and JavaScript frontend provides the interface for ingesting CVs, structuring jobs, managing API keys, and matching candidates.

projects.title: AI-Powered E-Learning Agent
projects.description: An AI-powered multi-agent assistant designed for an English e-learning platform. The system combines LLM reasoning with structured learning data, specialized tools, RAG, and conversational memory to provide context-aware and personalized responses.
projects.overview:
The assistant can handle different types of questions related to students, instructors, courses, exams, and educational content. Instead of relying entirely on the LLM, it connects the model to appropriate external sources and tools depending on the user's request.

The system also handles conversational context by retrieving relevant previous interactions or using a summarized conversation history when relevant information cannot be retrieved directly.
projects.problem:
An e-learning assistant needs to deal with several different sources of information:

- Structured student and course data
- Instructor information
- Unstructured educational documents
- Previous conversations
- User-specific permissions

A simple LLM-based chatbot cannot reliably determine which source to use, maintain useful context across conversations, or safely access user-specific information.

The challenge was therefore to design an agentic system capable of selecting the appropriate tools, combining information from multiple sources, and maintaining relevant context without unnecessarily increasing the LLM context window.
projects.approach:
I designed a multi-agent architecture using LangGraph and LangChain.

Main Agent

The Main Agent is responsible for understanding the user's request, selecting the appropriate tools, combining their outputs, and generating the final response.

It can work with:

Student tools for profiles, progress, summaries, and recommendations
Learning tools for course statistics, enrollment, and exams
Instructor tools for instructor information
RAG for retrieving information from educational documents
RAG

For unstructured educational knowledge, I implemented a Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline using embeddings and ChromaDB.

The process is:

User Question → Semantic Retrieval → Relevant Documents → LLM → Natural-Language Answer

Multiple relevant documents can be retrieved and combined when answering questions that require information from different sources.

Context & Memory

A dedicated History Agent was implemented to handle long-term conversational context.

Rather than sending the entire conversation history to the Main Agent, the History Agent:

Searches the vector database for semantically relevant previous interactions.
Returns only conversations above a relevance threshold.
Falls back to a summarized conversation history when relevant interactions cannot be retrieved.
Produces a concise context that is passed to the Main Agent.

This approach reduces unnecessary context while preserving useful information from previous interactions.

Permissions & Entity Resolution

The system also handles practical issues such as:

Role-based access to student information
Restricting students to their own data
Fuzzy matching for misspelled student names
Detecting ambiguous names when multiple students have the same name
Combining tool-generated information with general LLM knowledge when appropriate

projects.title: Poem Genre Classification Project
projects.description: A Natural Language Processing (NLP) project that classifies poems into one of four genres: Affection, Death, Environment, and Music. The project explores text representation learning by fine-tuning a transformer-based embedding model to improve semantic understanding and genre classification performance.
projects.overview: The Poem Genre Classification Project is a multi-class NLP classification system developed to automatically predict the genre of a poem based on its content. I experimented with multiple approaches, including traditional machine learning methods, pretrained sentence embeddings, fine-tuned embeddings, and artificial neural networks. Many of these approaches showed signs of overfitting and limited generalization. The final solution combines a fine-tuned Sentence Transformer embedding model with a Linear SVM classifier, producing more generalized predictions on unseen data.
projects.problem: Poetry often contains figurative language, metaphors, and overlapping themes, making genre classification a challenging NLP task. Poems from different genres may share similar vocabulary while expressing different meanings, reducing the effectiveness of traditional text representations and classifiers. The main challenge was therefore not only achieving high training performance, but also obtaining a model that generalizes well to unseen poems rather than overfitting the training data.
projects.approach: The project explored several approaches, including traditional machine learning models, pretrained sentence embeddings, fine-tuned embeddings, and artificial neural networks. These experiments showed that several configurations could achieve strong training performance but suffered from overfitting and weaker generalization on unseen data. The final approach uses a fine-tuned Sentence Transformer embedding model to learn representations specialized for poem genres, followed by a Linear SVM classifier. This combination provided a better balance between training and unseen-data performance. The final model achieved 76.67% Accuracy, 83.20% Precision, 76.67% Recall, and 78.33% weighted F1-Score on the test set, while the corresponding training metrics are also tracked to demonstrate the reduction in overfitting and improved generalization. The models were evaluated using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score on both training and test data.

projects.title: Spam classification
projects.description: A machine learning project that automatically classifies email and text messages as Spam or Not Spam (Ham). The system combines Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques with a Naive Bayes classifier to detect unwanted messages and improve communication security.
projects.overview: The Spam Detection System is a binary text classification application designed to identify spam messages based on their textual content. The project utilizes TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency) to convert text into numerical features that capture the importance of words within messages. These features are then used by a Naive Bayes model to distinguish between legitimate and spam communications with strong classification performance.
projects.problem: Spam messages continue to be a major challenge in digital communication, causing security concerns, reduced productivity, and poor user experience. Building an effective spam filter requires accurately identifying unwanted messages while avoiding the incorrect classification of legitimate communications. Additionally, imbalanced datasets can negatively impact model performance and lead to biased predictions.
projects.approach: The project begins with text preprocessing, including data cleaning, removal of unnecessary characters, and stemming. The textual data is then transformed into numerical representations using TF-IDF vectorization, which highlights important terms while reducing the influence of commonly occurring words. During exploratory analysis, the dataset was found to be imbalanced, so balancing techniques were applied to improve the model's ability to learn from both classes effectively. A Naive Bayes classifier was then trained on the TF-IDF features to perform binary classification. Model performance was evaluated using Accuracy (overall prediction correctness), Precision (the proportion of predicted spam messages that were actually spam), and Recall (the proportion of actual spam messages successfully identified). The final model achieved 93.4% Accuracy, 92.8% Precision, and 91.9% Recall, demonstrating strong performance in distinguishing spam from legitimate communications while maintaining a balance between false positives and missed spam messages.

projects.title: Email generator
projects.description: An AI-powered email generation tool that creates professional and personalized emails based on user-defined requirements. The application leverages LangChain and the Gemini API to generate complete emails, including both the subject line and body, while adapting to the desired style, tone, emotion, and communication context.
projects.overview: The Email Generator is a Generative AI application designed to simplify email writing by transforming user instructions into well-structured and context-aware emails. Users can provide details such as the sender's name, email purpose, target audience, writing style, emotional tone, and key points to include. The system then generates a polished email with an appropriate subject line, helping users save time while maintaining effective communication.
projects.problem: Writing professional emails can be time-consuming, especially when users need to adapt their message to different contexts, audiences, and tones. Many individuals struggle to find the right wording or structure for formal, persuasive, friendly, or emotionally sensitive communications. This challenge becomes more significant when frequent email creation is required, leading to reduced productivity and inconsistent messaging.
projects.approach: The project utilizes LangChain as the orchestration framework and the Gemini API as the underlying large language model. Users provide customization parameters such as the sender's name, email context, target audience, writing style, tone, emotion, and additional instructions. These inputs are incorporated into a carefully designed prompt that guides the model to generate a coherent and contextually appropriate email. The system then produces both a relevant subject line and a complete email body tailored to the user's requirements, ensuring consistency, clarity, and personalization.

projects.title: Customer Churn Prediction
projects.description: A machine learning project that predicts customer churn in the banking sector and segments customers into distinct groups based on their behavioral and demographic characteristics. The system combines predictive analytics, customer segmentation, and generative AI-powered recommendations to help banks identify at-risk customers and improve retention strategies.
projects.overview: The Customer Churn Prediction System is designed to analyze customer data and determine the likelihood of a customer leaving the bank. In addition to churn prediction, the project uses clustering techniques to segment customers into meaningful groups, enabling more targeted retention strategies. To enhance decision-making, a recommendation module built with LangChain and the Gemini API generates actionable insights and personalized recommendations based on the prediction and segmentation results.
projects.problem: Customer churn represents a significant challenge for banks, as acquiring new customers is often more expensive than retaining existing ones. Identifying customers who are likely to leave and understanding the characteristics of different customer segments are essential for developing effective retention strategies. Traditional analysis methods may fail to uncover complex patterns in customer behavior, making it difficult to proactively address churn risks.
projects.approach: The project follows a complete data science workflow, starting with data preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, and feature engineering to prepare customer data for modeling. A Random Forest Classifier was trained to predict customer churn, with the final performance achieved after multiple iterations of hyperparameter tuning and experimentation. The final model achieved 85.43% Accuracy, 85.71% Precision, 85.28% Recall, and 85.49% F1-Score on the training set, and 81.98% Accuracy, 81.36% Precision, 82.23% Recall, and 81.79% F1-Score on the test set. These results demonstrate the model's ability to generalize to unseen customer data. For customer segmentation, K-Means clustering was applied, and the optimal number of clusters was selected using the Silhouette Score, which measures how well customers fit within their assigned clusters. Finally, LangChain integrated with the Gemini API was used to generate personalized recommendations and retention strategies based on each customer's predicted churn risk and segment profile.

projects.title: ROP Prediction System
projects.description: A freelance machine learning project developed for the oil and gas industry to predict the Rate of Penetration (ROP) during drilling operations. The system leverages historical drilling and geological data to estimate drilling performance, helping engineers optimize operational parameters and improve drilling efficiency.
projects.overview: The ROP Prediction System is a predictive analytics solution designed to forecast drilling penetration rates based on operational and formation-related parameters. By applying machine learning techniques to drilling data, the system provides accurate ROP estimates that can support decision-making, reduce drilling time, and improve overall well performance.
projects.problem: Rate of Penetration is one of the most important indicators of drilling efficiency. However, ROP is influenced by numerous interacting factors, including drilling parameters, mud properties, and geological formations. Predicting ROP accurately using traditional empirical methods is challenging, often resulting in suboptimal drilling decisions, increased costs, and reduced operational efficiency.
projects.approach: The project began with data preprocessing and exploratory analysis, followed by feature engineering to create meaningful variables from drilling parameters and improve predictive performance. Several regression models were then trained and compared, including linear and tree-based approaches. After evaluation, Random Forest Regressor achieved the best results and was further optimized through hyperparameter tuning. The final model achieved an R² Score of 87.04%, with an RMSE of 6.64, MAE of 3.95, and MAPE of 0.23. Model performance was assessed using R² Score (how well the model explains variations in ROP), MAE (average absolute prediction error), RMSE (penalizes larger prediction errors), and MAPE (average percentage error). The final model was integrated into an interactive application for real-time ROP prediction.

projects.title: House Price Estimator
projects.overview: House Price Estimator is a machine learning project that predicts the price of a house using its features, such as area, number of bedrooms, bathrooms, and other relevant attributes. The project implements a Linear Regression model from scratch in Python to demonstrate the fundamental concepts behind predictive modeling without relying on machine learning frameworks.
projects.problem: Estimating house prices accurately is important for buyers, sellers, and real estate agencies. Manual valuation can be subjective and time-consuming, making it difficult to determine a fair market price based on multiple property characteristics.
projects.approach: The project follows a complete machine learning workflow, starting with data preprocessing and feature selection to prepare the housing data for training. A Linear Regression model is then implemented entirely from scratch using Python and NumPy, with gradient descent used to learn the optimal parameters by minimizing prediction error. The model achieved an R² Score of 89.12% on the training set and 86.47% on the test set, demonstrating reasonable generalization to unseen properties. Performance was evaluated using Mean Squared Error (MSE), which measures the average squared prediction error, and R² Score, which measures how well the model explains the variation in house prices. The trained model is finally used to predict house prices based on the features of unseen properties.
